_about: THE WRITER REGISTRY (ledger #345). David's rule, 2026-09-17: single functions that are called, repeatable, dependable and verifiable; the test for each verifies, from capture to write, that each path is validated; and any change to the writer re-runs the same validation from every capture/change form to the database, so there are no gaps.
One entry per DOMAIN: its writer, the tables it owns, and EVERY place a person (or an import, OCR, script or endpoint) can enter or change that domain's data, each with the id of its end-to-end test.

`npm run verify:writer-registry` (scripts/verify-writer-registry.mjs) fails the build when: a file in packages/, api/ or scripts/ looks like a capture path for a registered domain and is neither a path's file nor declared; a path's test is missing or failing; code writes a registered table outside the writer's files; a declaration or anchor has gone stale.
`at` is `file#anchor`: the verifier resolves the anchor to a line number on every run and prints file:line, so the number cannot drift from the code.
Read this file before touching any form, capture, import or endpoint (CLAUDE.md §10 step 12).

domains.title: What happened at a stop — Start, Done, Undo, Note — through ONE completion writer, from either door (ledger #347)

writer.name: stop_progress_apply (database) — reached by crew_stop_act (token) and stop_act (session)

guardedColumns.databaseGuard: Set only inside stop_progress_apply (20260917c §4b) — the ONE completion writer. Both doors call it: crew_stop_act (token, the link's own day) and stop_act (a logged-in member with deliveries:update). David's ruling 2026-09-17: both doors HOLD the review ask and both are undoable. NOT a trigger: stopWrites.ts still writes delivery_date and the ship-to on the same row through RLS, which is a different operation. The route columns (route_position / routed_at / routed_by) are written only by save_route_order (20260917e) — the one writer for the day's plan, ledger #351. ✏️ PIECE 2 (20260923b, [[R-169]]): the route columns are still save_route_order's alone, but the re-route CLEAR is now scoped to the team being routed — `team_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM p_team_id`. The day-scoped clear is what wiped Team 2's order on Saturday 2026-09-19 (tech-debt #345). `delivery_route_plans` holds one row per team per day with the optimiser's OWN miles and minutes, kept as a snapshot and never recomputed.

domains.databaseGuardForTables: BUILT: neither table has an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE policy, and the migration revokes those privileges from anon and authenticated. Every write is inside a SECURITY DEFINER function (create_crew_day_link, revoke_crew_day_link, crew_stop_act). crew_stop_act and crew_day_read can be called only by service_role — the endpoint.

domains.databaseGuardForTables: APPEND-ONLY, AND ENFORCED TWICE. `trg_rung_dates_immutable` (20260924a) raises on any UPDATE or DELETE, and the table carries NO update and NO delete policy for anyone, owner included. So unlike `contacts`, the database itself refuses a correction-by-edit — a correction is a NEW ROW. What the database cannot tell is the writer's INSERT from any other; RLS (`inventory:update`) is that guard.
